Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT or Tl INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 42 S. 2mo 12 April 2010 MR. AUGUSTO C. TOLENTINO Board President AKLAN ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE INC. (AKELCO) Lezo, Aklan Dear Mr. Tolentino: Presented before this Department is a query by Aklan Electric Cooperative (AKELCO) seeking legal opinion on whether the act of the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of Kalibo, Province of Aklan in issuing Resolution No. 2007-01 entitled: "Calling the National Electrification Administration and the Members of the Board of Directors of the Aklan Electric Cooperative for the Immediate Holding of Elections of a Member to the Board of the Aklan Electric Cooperative (AKELCO) Representing District TV, Composed of the Municipalities of Kalibo and Numancia", is deemed an interference in the affairs of AKELCO. The legal authorities used by AKELCO as reference were the case of I Electric vs Sangguniang Panlalawigan of 'Negros Occidental Dumaguete', DILG Opinion Nos. 3-1994, 212-1993, and 11-19921. The abovecited ruling and opinions referred to the propriety of compulsory processes issued by a local legislative body. This was also reiterated in DILG Opinion No. 22, Series of 2009 dated 18 May 2009, wherein in essence, the Department rendered its legal view that "in the exercise of legislative powers, the sanggunian has no compulsory process to require persons to appear before it"2 (citing the same case of Negros Oriental II Electric Cooperative) and "in the exercise of quasi-judicial functions, the sanggunian can compel the appearance of any person pursuant to its subpoena powers in relation to Section 65 of the Local Government Code of 1991( Rights of Respondent)."3. Copy of the said DILG opinion is hereto attached for your reference. 2 3 Machine copy of 'Page 54, Compendium of Decisions, Rulings, Resolutions, and Opinions on Local Autonomy and Local Government' attached to the letter request Fifth Paragraph, Page l, Opinion No, 22-2009 Third Paragraph, Page 3 (Last Page), Ibid.

Your query, however, particularly refers to the act of the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of Kalibo, Province of Aklan calling the National Electrification Authority (NEA) to immediately hold an election of a member to the Board of AKELCO. In resolving your query, we cite the case of National Electrification Authority (NEA) vs Mationg4 wherein the Supreme Court held that the "NEA, as a public corporation, exercises supervision and control over electric cooperatives organized and operating under the mandate of PD 269, as amended. The extent of government control . over electric cooperatives covered by PD 269, as amended, is largely a function of the NEA a.s a primary source of fimds of these electric cooperatives". The power of control and supervision by NEA over all electric cooperatives in the country is reiterated in the latter case of Zambales II Electric Inc. Board of Directors vs Castillejos 5 wherein the Supreme upheld the Consumers Association Inc. continuing regulatory power of the NEA to control and supervise electric cooperatives despite the passage of the Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001 (EPIRA): "The passage of the EPIRA and its creation of PSALM Corp. which assumed all outstanding Tillancial obligations of electric cooperatives did not (1ffi'Ct the power of the NEA particularly over administrative cases involving the board of directors, officers and employees of electric cooperatives. This authority is expressly recognized l/"der [he Iasi paragraph of Sec. 58, Chapter of the EPIRA which states thuf, "NEA shall continue to be under the supervision of the DOE and shall exercise its functions under Presidential Decree No. 269 as amended fry Presidential Decree No. 1645 are with this Act. " (emphasis and consistent underscoring supplied) Pursuant to the exercise of this regulatory powers over electric cooperatives, NEA had issued a Memorandum dated 09 July 1993, addressed to all Regional Electrification Managers and Electric Cooperatives providing for the 'Guidelines on the Conduct of EC District Elections', or the 1993 Electric Cooperative Election Code. Considering the foregoing premises, it is the view of this Department that clearly, the power of regulation and control by NEA over all electric cooperatives as so provided by law cannot be undermined by a mere resolution of a local legislative body which is 'merely a G.R. No. 160174, 28 August 2006 5 G.R. No. 176935-36, 13 March 2009 2

declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matter'6. It is axiomatic that the clear letter of the law is controlling and cannot he amended by administrative issued for its implementation7. Thus, on matters involving the conduct of election among electric cooperatives, it is the NEA which primari!y possesses that authority, to the exclusion of all others. We hope that this settles your concerns with finality. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: AVTY. JESUS . DOQ E Director III Copy Furnished: ASEC Rolando M.
